digest.component_or_area: acceptance criteria tagging and evidence-kind classification
propositions: The tag [operator-attested] is semantically misleading because 'operator' signals a human actor when agents can attest equally; the name should reflect WHERE evidence lives (outside codebase) not WHO attests

Both [non-codebase] and [operator-attested] must be recognized identically across deterministic matchers, verifiers, guards, and close paths, with the regex widened to a non-capturing alternation to preserve findall() arity
Legacy persisted verdicts with kind:'operator-attested' must render identically to new kind:'non-codebase' verdicts; the reader site must widen before emitter cutover to avoid silent reclassification
The .rebar/criteria_routing.json activation trigger and all prompts must accept both spellings to prevent [non-codebase]-tagged plans from silently skipping project.measurement-provenance
Author-facing guidance and emitted classifications must use [non-codebase] only; [operator-attested] is retained as an undocumented compatibility alias for 827 immutable event-sourced tickets
Contract text selectors, digest pins, generated guide regeneration, and all CI gates must be updated atomically with prompt and code changes to maintain parity and prevent false test failures
